=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:192-195 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prefix filter skips only dot-prefixed parts, secret/credential names and non-build EXCLUDED names. allowed() also hides parts ending in .pem, .key, .p12, .pfx, .keystore, .egg-info and .dist-info, so paths like `certs.pem/build/x.txt` pass and their directory name reaches the prompt note.
  WHY: This breaks the "names only, nothing hidden for another reason" contract. Impact is limited to the directory name.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:hidden_build_note() 210-220 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The note caps entries at 40 but not the length of each key, and keys come from PR-controlled paths.
  WHY: Long paths put PR-authored text into the unfenced prompt section, which inflates the prompt and is a small injection channel.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:184 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The charset check runs on the whole file path rather than the key, so files with spaces, non-ASCII, @, +, [, ], ~ or $ are skipped.
  WHY: Counts are too low, and a directory whose files all have such names is never listed, so the #4770 misreading persists.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:399 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The count includes tracked paths not present as regular files in the host worktree, such as unstaged deletions.
  WHY: The note can report a count that is too high, but it is an upper bound and advisory only.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:201-234 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The note from hidden_build_note() is unbounded in size, so many or very long file paths under hidden build directories could push it past 160KB.
  WHY: The function lists all hidden build directories with no character or path length limit, which bloats the prompt and gives a prompt-injection or DoS vector.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:173-199 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prefix check for sensitive paths is insufficient. It does not cover sensitive file types such as .pem, .key, .pfx and .p12.
  WHY: A sensitive build file committed under dist/ or build/ would have its path included in the sandbox prompt note, leaking information.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:173-199 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The charset check re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+", name) is applied to the entire file path. Files with spaces, non-ASCII, @, +, [, ], ~ or $ are excluded from the count.
  WHY: The note understates the file count, and a dist/ directory whose files all have such names is not listed, defeating the #4770 fix.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: Implement a note in the sandbox prompt about hidden build directories. | Expected change site: scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh | Evidence of absence: The PR delivers the note but misses safeguards (length limits, robust path filtering, accurate file counting) required to make it safe and useful. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:193-194 (compare `_log_safe_dir` 111-117) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prefix filter reproduces only part of the rule allowed() applies at line 134 and omits the key-material suffixes that _log_safe_dir checks at line 115.
  WHY: A PR can commit `deploy.key/build/index.js`. allowed() hides it, but the key `deploy.key/build` is written to the sidecar and rendered at line 220 into the prompt.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:209-210, 220; scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh:405-407 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: MAX_HIDDEN_BUILD_NOTE_DIRS bounds the entry count but not the length of a single PR-controlled key. The note is appended with no UNTRUSTED_DATA framing.
  WHY: Git allows paths up to 4096 bytes, so 40 entries put roughly 160 KB of unfenced PR-authored text into every sandbox prompt. This is a hardening gap, not an injection hole.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:184, key built at 192-196 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ASCII charset test runs on the whole tracked file path, but only the prefix is printed, so files named like `app+a1b2.js`, `index copy.html` or `logo@2x.png` are skipped.
  WHY: A build tree whose files all have such names never reaches the sidecar, so the #4770 misreading survives, while README.md and agents.d/7921-…md claim "plain-ASCII paths only".
- changelog.d/7921-review-sandbox-hidden-build-dirs.md:12 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The changelog claim that "judges, reviewers and the review editor" are covered overstates scope. Only the PANEL_REVIEWER Claude-pool slot runs through review_untrusted_sandbox.sh run (scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:5303).
  WHY: This is not a code defect, but operators would expect the whole reviewer panel to be fixed. It should be narrowed to match line 2.
- (Hardening) scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:399 
  PROBLEM: The count comes from git ls-files, so a tracked path absent from the worktree (unstaged deletion) is counted although the snapshot skipped it at line 376.
  WHY: Suggested fix: pass `host` in and count only when `(host / name).exists()`, or drop the per-directory count. This was listed as hardening suggestion 4 only.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
